news.headline: October U.S. PPI Due Friday; Consensus at 6.6% YoY as Fed Hike Odds Rise
news.body: October PPI data is set for release at 8:30 a.m. ET on Friday, Nov. 13, with consensus forecasting a 6.6% year-over-year print — up from 6.3% in September — and a cooling 0.4% month-over-month headline versus the prior 1.3% spike. The report follows a hotter-than-expected October CPI print of 0.4% MoM released Nov. 10, which lifted Fed rate-hike odds for December. The 10-year Treasury yield stands near 5.04% and markets are pricing significant probability of a 25–50 bps December hike; a further PPI surprise would add additional pressure on rate-sensitive equities and growth stocks.

news.headline: Cisco Q1 FY2027 Revenue Hits Record $18.52B, Up 24%; Raises Full-Year Outlook
news.body: Cisco reported fiscal Q1 2027 revenue of $18.52 billion, surpassing the $18.12 billion consensus by ~2.2%, with non-GAAP EPS of $1.40 beating the $1.29 estimate by 8.5% and rising 40% year-over-year. Product revenue surged 32% to $14.67 billion, driven by AI infrastructure networking demand, and the company raised its fiscal 2027 guidance. Shares edged higher after hours, reinforcing the AI capex cycle thesis that extends well beyond chip makers into networking infrastructure. The beat comes alongside $9.3 billion in AI infrastructure orders received during all of fiscal 2026.

news.headline: Cerebras Systems Surges ~15% After-Hours on Revenue Beat and Microsoft Deal
news.body: Cerebras (CBRS) reported Q3 core revenue of $230.9 million, an 8% beat versus the $214.7 million consensus and +70% year-over-year growth, while issuing Q4 guidance of $310–$330 million that topped expectations. The company also announced a new hyperscaler deal with Microsoft, adding a major enterprise anchor. Shares jumped ~15% in extended trading after losing nearly half their value since the company's May 2026 IPO at $185; management guided for revenue to triple in 2027. The result adds further momentum to the AI inference chip theme alongside CoreWeave's blowout earlier in the week.

news.headline: Kraft Heinz Holds Investor Day on NYSE Debut; Projects Return to Growth in 2027
news.body: Kraft Heinz (KHC) hosted its 2026 Investor Day on Nov. 12, coinciding with its newly completed transfer from Nasdaq to the NYSE, where CEO Steve Cahillane outlined a strategy for volume-led profitable growth in developing and emerging markets. The company guided for relatively flat full-year organic net sales and a low-single-digit decline in adjusted operating income in 2026, with a return to growth projected for 2027. Shares rose ~2% on the day as investors welcomed the clearer strategic roadmap, though the stock remains loss-making with a negative TTM EPS, keeping valuation multiples unapplicable on an earnings basis.

news.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Immediately Amid Spy Scandal, Stock Off 20% in Nov.
news.body: Nvidia's board announced the immediate resignation of co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang on Nov. 12, citing affairs including one with a Chinese national suspected by U.S. intelligence of being a state asset. CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO, with Harvey C. Jones appointed board chairman. NVDA closed down 4.34% on the day and is off roughly 20% in November alone, dragging the Nasdaq and S&P 500 lower; Congress opened a probe and the FBI is separately investigating. Markets face continued uncertainty around Nvidia's AI chip strategy and pending Hugging Face acquisition following the leadership void.

news.headline: Japan Megabanks MUFG, SMFG & Mizuho Report H1 Earnings on BOJ-Rate Tailwind
news.body: All three of Japan's megabanks — MUFG, Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group and Mizuho — held their Q2 FY2027 earnings calls on November 13, with Q1 net income of ¥809.4 billion, ¥501.3 billion and ¥422.9 billion respectively, putting Mizuho at 32.5% and SMFG at 29.5% of full-year targets ahead of a linear run rate. BOJ rate normalisation continues to widen net interest margins, while SMFG's first-half records across gross profit, net business profit and net income reinforce the case for further full-year upgrades. The results are a key catalyst for Japan bank stocks on a day the Nikkei gains 1.6%, sustaining investor expectations for a BOJ December rate hike now priced at ~82%.

news.headline: Singtel H1 Underlying Profit Rises 10% to S$1.49B; Dividend Up 10%
news.body: Singapore Telecommunications reported first-half FY2027 underlying net profit of S$1.49 billion, up 10.4% year-on-year, driven by double-digit EBIT growth at Optus, NCS and Digital InfraCo, plus higher contributions from regional associates Bharti Airtel and AIS. The company raised its full-year EBIT guidance and declared an interim dividend of 9.0 Singapore cents per share — up 10% from 8.2 cents — totalling about S$1.47 billion payable in December. Singtel has now repurchased and cancelled ~S$1 billion of shares under its S$2 billion buyback, and capital recycling has unlocked S$6.8 billion toward a S$9 billion mid-term target, lifting STI sentiment for dividend-growth plays.

news.headline: Alibaba Sinks 7% as U.S. Moves to Curb China Remote AI Chip Access
news.body: U.S.-listed Chinese tech stocks fell sharply on November 12 after reports that Washington is finalizing restrictions on China's remote access to advanced AI chips via cloud platforms. Alibaba dropped ~7%, Baidu fell ~4%, and PDD slid ~3% on the Nasdaq Golden Dragon China Index, which declined over 3%. Hong Kong-listed Tencent and Alibaba H-shares also fell. The dual pressure from the AI chip access curbs and tepid Singles' Day sales data underscored investor concern over China's tech sector growth ceiling.

news.headline: SMIC Q3 Profit More Than Doubles to $428M on Record $3.19B Revenue
news.body: China's Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp reported a 123.4% jump in third-quarter net profit to $428.4 million on November 12, beating the $418.4 million consensus, while revenue surged 33.9% to a record $3.19 billion, topping the $3.09 billion forecast. Gross margin hit 29.9%, up from 25.3% in Q2, and utilisation reached 97.3%; co-CEO Zhao Haijun guided Q4 sequential revenue growth of 4–6% and raised the full-year revenue outlook to above $12 billion, up nearly 30% year-on-year. The blowout result underscores China's domestic chip localisation drive and AI-linked demand, reinforcing the bull case for Hong Kong-listed semiconductor stocks despite ongoing U.S. export restrictions on advanced equipment.

news.headline: TSMC, SK Hynix Slide as Jensen Huang Quits Nvidia Amid Scandal
news.body: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigned as president and CEO on November 11, 2026, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO and Harvey C. Jones appointed first-ever board chair. TSMC shares fell 2% and SK Hynix dropped 1.6% on the news, as investors fretted over the loss of Nvidia's most aggressive champion of Taiwan investment, though Samsung Electronics edged up 0.8%. Taiwan suppliers say near-term demand for Vera Rubin and Feynman platforms is intact, but warn that a successor may not sustain Huang's pace of ecosystem-level deals and supply-chain commitments worth ~$150bn annually in Taiwan.

news.headline: Copper Hits Three-Month Low Near $6.20/lb as AI Demand Rethink and Rate Fears Converge
news.body: Copper futures fell to $6.20/lb on November 12 — the lowest in at least three months and down 7.15% over the past month — as markets reassessed the magnitude of AI-infrastructure-driven demand following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation. The CPER copper ETF closed at $37.24, its third consecutive daily loss and 10.1% below its September peak. Rising U.S. interest rates, a firmer dollar, and weak Chinese demand signals compounded the sell-off in base metals broadly; LME copper inventories rose by 3,050 tonnes on November 11. Copper bounced fractionally in Asian trade on November 13, suggesting oversold technicals, but macro headwinds from Fed tightening and demand uncertainty keep the outlook pressured.

news.headline: Gold Extends Decline to 13-Month Low as Fed Hike Bets and Oil Pressures Mount
news.body: Spot gold slid nearly 3% intraday on November 12 to around $3,870/oz, its lowest level in approximately 13 months, dragged down by a hotter-than-expected October CPI, a firmer U.S. dollar, and 10-year Treasury yields approaching 5%. CME FedWatch now prices ~88.8% odds of a 25bp December Fed hike, with 11.2% odds for a 50bp move after Fed Governor Waller signaled readiness for more aggressive tightening. ANZ analysts flagged that rising energy costs, stronger economic data, and a dollar above 103 have collectively weakened investment demand for bullion. Gold has shed roughly 4.65% over the past month and is down over 30% from its January 2026 all-time high of $5,608.

news.headline: Houthis Strike Saudi East-West Pipeline and Yanbu Oil Facility; Brent Surges 3.5%
news.body: Yemen's Houthi forces claimed drone and ballistic missile strikes on November 12 against Pumping Station No. 7 on Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline and an oil facility in the Red Sea port of Yanbu, as well as an Aramco building in Riyadh. Brent crude surged 3.49% to settle near $96/bbl and WTI gained 2.6% to ~$88.74, reversing earlier session losses as supply-risk premium was rapidly repriced. The East-West Pipeline is now routing roughly 4 million barrels per day — about 4% of global supply — after Hormuz Strait disruptions, making it a critical chokepoint. Saudi Arabia's military coalition said it intercepted and destroyed two Houthi drones, but structural supply-disruption risk remains elevated.
news.source: Reuters / Cyprus Mail / Middle East Eye

news.headline: EU TTF Natural Gas Jumps 7-8% to Two-Week High on Norwegian Outages and Low Storage
news.body: European TTF natural gas prices surged 7–8% on November 12 to above €93–95/MWh, the highest in two weeks, compounding a year-on-year gain of over 206%. Unplanned outages at Norway's Troll and Åsgard fields cut Norwegian pipeline deliveries roughly 9% below year-ago levels, while EU storage fell below 72% capacity versus a five-year seasonal average of 89%, with German inventories below 60%. Trump's rejection of an Iran deal and reduced Qatari LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz further tightened the winter supply outlook. Forecasts of a cold snap from November 17 and ENTSOG modeling showing inventories could end winter near 10% full under a cold scenario amplified the move.

news.headline: Silver Drops 3%+ to Near $50/oz as Dollar Surge and Fed Tightening Fears Bite
news.body: Spot silver fell 3.23% to around $50/oz on November 12, its lowest close in recent months and extending a 15.5% monthly decline, the sharpest one-month drop among major precious metals. The sell-off mirrors gold's but is amplified by silver's dual role as both a monetary and industrial metal, with copper simultaneously dropping ~1.2% to a three-month low of $6.20/lb as AI-sector demand assumptions are revised lower following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation. Fed Governor Waller's hawkish signals and an October CPI print of +0.4% MoM drove December hike odds to ~88.8%, raising the opportunity cost of non-yielding metals. Traders now await Friday's October PPI data, with headline PPI expected at 6.6% YoY, as the next key inflation test for precious metals.
